````markdown
## 4. Engine grants

Before an installation restarts with `table_engines_require_grant`, every user of it that creates tables holds its engines by name (K41): `si_snode` and `si_verifier` exactly `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`, `si_gateway` the census's set `ENGINE_CENSUS` (`Memory`, `MergeTree` and the tenant engines, never a `Replicated*` engine), `si_reader` and `si_backup` none, `default` and `clickhouse_operator` untouched. Each grant is one `GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON <Engine>` appended to that user's `grants/query`; never `ON *` and never a revoke. While the setting is off the grants change nothing, and a users change only reloads, so each installation is one window of its own with the proof that nothing restarted. Order: indexer-b, indexer-c, network (the network installation's reload reaches its source and the three verifier ClickHouses). Each window is three blocks: the baseline (read-only), the commit (local), and one confirmed block that pushes, applies or syncs and then checks, read-only, that the grants arrived and nothing restarted.

## 5. Restart windows

Each SI ClickHouse restarts exactly once, carrying the whole bundle (K39): `zz-si-access-control.xml` (`table_engines_require_grant`), `zz-si-storage.xml` (`keep_free_space_bytes` on every disk, the disk and policy `member`; indexer-c keeps Plan S3-B Task 19's file, which has both already), `zz-si-replicated-merge-tree.xml` (the merge default 0), `zz-si-named-collections.xml` (`NOT OVERRIDABLE` collections) and `zz-pool-settings.xml` (`background_fetches_pool_size` 16), with the reader environment from the reader Secrets, in one commit and one apply, so the operator restarts each pod once. The order is indexer-b, indexer-c, network; never two windows in one session, and a restart never rides with any other change.

A window, as contract §27.5 binds it: the quiet point (`si_quiet_point`), the commit (local), then in one confirmed block the push, the apply and `si_restart_watch` until every pod of the installation restarted once and the CHI is `Completed`; then, read-only, each pod's single restart, `si_p2_stage_check <host> restarted` on every pod, the owner audit's `clickhouse_restart` run (`sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_runs_total{trigger="clickhouse_restart"}` up by one and `unclean_tables` 0); then, confirmed, the 497 probe (as `si_gateway` on the owner's source, a `CREATE TABLE … ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree` refused with 497 naming `TABLE ENGINE ON ReplicatedMergeTree`, with no znode under `p2-restart-probe`, the order §3 measured); one acceptance write of that owner that reaches safe; and, read-only, the window's record `restart-<installation>.txt`. During the window the owner's tables answer `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` and then Pending (733) until the audit is clean; both are retryable. For the network window also: every block sealed during the window reaches a verdict with quorum, and no track is quarantined.

### 5.1 indexer-b

Read-only: the quiet point (contract §27.5) and the baseline; run it again if the window does not start within 10 minutes:

```bash
# block p2-5-1-1
hosts='b'
{
  si_quiet_point b
  si_chi_state storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b | tee "$si_backup/chi-indexer-b-restart-before.txt"
  si_audit b | tee "$si_backup/audit-b-restart-before.txt"
  for h in $hosts; do si_p2_stage_check "$h" engines; done

  echo "the arbiter and verifier pods are the same"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/restart-network-checks.txt"

## 6. The unsafe_inc root

Spec §8.2 requires `/sentio/<shard>/unsafe_inc` to exist before any member user exists, and devnet2's Keeper shard id is 0 (arbiter-core `dataplane/ddl/naming.go:44-46`), so between the last restart window and the first `si_member` this section creates `/storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2/sentio/0/unsafe_inc`, the network's Keeper root plus `/sentio/0/unsafe_inc`, which every SI installation shares (K42). No reconciler ever creates it and nothing removes it: it stays an empty plain znode until stage 3 P6's `purge` switch scopes new incarnations under it, and an empty znode changes nothing for any existing table. `clickhouse-keeper-client` 26.3 rejects `create '<path>' ''` as a syntax error and exits 0 on every command, so the block creates the node with `touch` (an empty value) and proves it with `ls`; it stops if the node exists without this runbook's record of creating it.

Read-only, first:

```bash
# block p2-6-1
[ -s "$si_backup/p2-restart-end.txt" ] || { echo "the restart windows have not ended (§5.3): stop"; exit 1; }
listing="$(si_keeper "ls '$si_p2_root/sentio/0'")"
case "$listing" in *"No node"*|*rror*) echo "cannot list $si_p2_root/sentio/0: $listing"; exit 1 ;; esac
echo "children of $si_p2_root/sentio/0: $listing"
case " $listing " in
  *" unsafe_inc "*)
    children="$(si_unsafe_inc | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    [ -z "$children" ] || { echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc exists with children ($children): stop and ask (K42)"; exit 1; }
    grep -q '^created ' "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt" 2> /dev/null || { echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc exists empty without this runbook's record of creating it: stop and ask (K42)"; exit 1; }
    echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc exists empty after its recorded creation: skip the create, run the record block" ;;
  *) echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc does not exist yet: the create block may run" ;;
esac
```

Expected: the listing of `/sentio/0` (the `unsafe` path the SNodes' `hg_unsafe` replicas use) without `unsafe_inc`, and `… does not exist yet: the create block may run`.

Confirm before running.

```bash
# block p2-6-2
[ -s "$si_backup/p2-restart-end.txt" ] || { echo "the restart windows have not ended (§5.3): stop"; exit 1; }
[ ! -s "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt" ] || { echo "§6 ran already: read $si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt"; exit 1; }
parent="$(si_keeper "ls '$si_p2_root/sentio/0'")"
case "$parent" in *"No node"*|*rror*) echo "cannot list $si_p2_root/sentio/0: $parent"; exit 1 ;; esac
case " $parent " in *" unsafe_inc "*) echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc exists without this runbook's record of creating it: stop and ask (K42)"; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$(si_p2_keeper_exists "$si_p2_unsafe_inc")" = 0 ] || { echo "unsafe_inc exists or is unreadable: stop (K42)"; exit 1; }
si_keeper "touch '$si_p2_unsafe_inc'"
[ "$(si_p2_keeper_exists "$si_p2_unsafe_inc")" = 1 ] || { echo "unsafe_inc touch outcome unknown: stop, never repeat blindly"; exit 1; }
echo "created $si_p2_unsafe_inc $(si_stamp) UTC" | tee "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt"
```

Then, read-only (safe to re-run), the proof and the record; its last line is `UNSAFE_INC_ROOT`, which this plan's live task records:

```bash
# block p2-6-3
grep -q '^created ' "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt" || { echo "no record of creating unsafe_inc: run the block above"; exit 1; }
listing="$(si_keeper "ls '$si_p2_root/sentio/0'")"
case " $listing " in *" unsafe_inc "*) ;; *) echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc does not exist ($listing): stop"; exit 1 ;; esac
children="$(si_unsafe_inc | tr -d '[:space:]')"
[ -z "$children" ] || { echo "$si_p2_unsafe_inc has children ($children): stop and ask (K42)"; exit 1; }
grep -qxF "UNSAFE_INC_ROOT=$si_p2_unsafe_inc" "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt" || {
  echo "children of $si_p2_root/sentio/0: $listing"
  echo "unsafe_inc is an empty plain znode"
  echo "UNSAFE_INC_ROOT=$si_p2_unsafe_inc"
} >> "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt"
cat "$si_backup/unsafe-inc.txt"
```

Expected: `created …`, the listing with `unsafe` (the legacy path the SNodes' `hg_unsafe` replicas use) and `unsafe_inc`, `unsafe_inc is an empty plain znode`, and the last line `UNSAFE_INC_ROOT=/storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2/sentio/0/unsafe_inc`.

## 7. Member users

`si_member` (spec §8.2 as amended, decision D36) exists on an installation only from its `member` stage, after its restart (§5) and after `UNSAFE_INC_ROOT` (§6): exactly the sixteen grants of `SI_MEMBER_GRANTS` (Plan S3-C2 contract §23.2) with one `GRANT NAMED COLLECTION ON <collection>` per collection of that installation before `GRANT READ ON REMOTE`, its literal SHA-256 hash, `networks/ip` `::/0` and the profile `si_member` (`max_memory_usage` 4 GiB, `max_concurrent_queries_for_user` 8, `max_threads` 4, `priority` 10). Its `hg_rstage` right names `SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, OPTIMIZE` and is never `ALL`. `si_member_ddl` is not created anywhere before stage 3 P6 step 6. A users reload: each installation is its own window with the proof that nothing restarted, in the order indexer-b, indexer-c, network; then §7.4 probes every SI ClickHouse as `si_member`.

### 7.4 Member probe

Every SI ClickHouse, as `si_member`, against the live collections of its installation: the refusal-only corpus `charts/storage-integrity/tests/si_member_live_probe.tsv` (the sixteen `Replicated*MergeTree` rows, the eight reaching-engine rows, the `Replicated` database row, the table-free `hg_rstage` creation rows, `INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote(si_owner_<id>, …)` and the four overrides), every row `denied` (497) or `override` (36), and each refused `CREATE TABLE … ENGINE = <X>` naming `TABLE ENGINE ON <X>`. No si-member runs yet, so the probe creates `hg_rstage` and `hg_replica` as `si_member` and drops them again on each host. The statements are refused, but they are DDL and an `INSERT` on live hosts, so each installation's probe is a confirmed block of its own (indexer-b, indexer-c, then the network installation's four ClickHouses):

Confirm before running.

```bash

Expected: `member probe ok on <host> (<n> rows)` for `b`, `c`, `a`, `v1`, `v2` and `v3`, the same `<n>` six times, and `$si_backup/member-probe-<host>.tsv` with every row's `got` equal to its `expect`. A row that was accepted (its object is dropped again by the helper) or answered otherwise: stop; the users or the bundle of that installation are wrong, and §13 reverts its `member` stage.

## 8. si-members

One si-member per SI indexer host, each in its own StatefulSet `<release>-si-member` of the host's sentio-node release (never in the host pod): its own ConfigMap `<release>-si-member-config` and pod annotation `checksum/si-member-config`, its own state volume (`/data/si-member`), the digest-pinned member image, the `si_member` password from `storage-integrity-si-v2-member-<installation>` and the restore key of stage 3 P1 in the `si-member` container only, the status token from its own Secret, metrics on 9095 and the reserved status port 9096 on Service `<release>-si-member`, and the reconciler slot off. Its config names the host's own source ClickHouse, every other SI indexer as a peer through its `si_owner_<id>` collection, the pool verifiers' collections, the P1 bucket as restore source, `shadow_verification: true`, `storage_policy: member`, `stop_installs_ratio` 0.5 and `disk_budget_bytes` = the member disk's total of §1.2, so installs pause at half the member disk (decision D28, K40). Off consensus: a member reads the watermark, manifests, block verifications, the registry and DA payloads, and writes only its own `hg_replica` and `hg_rstage` tables on the member disk.

Order: `member-b` (indexer-b), `member-c` (indexer-c), `member-a` (indexer-a); one member per window, each a single-service commit of its host overlay with `DEVNET2_MEMBERS_ENABLED` and a sync of that release only. Starting a member changes nothing in the host pod: the render diff names only the three member objects, and the host pod's uid and restart count and the host StatefulSet's generation and revision stay the same.

### 8.4 Monitoring

Once all three members run, one commit lists them for monitoring: `monitoring.members.releases` = the three host releases, `monitoring.members.installations` = the three CHIs (with `DEVNET2_MONITORED_MEMBERS` and `DEVNET2_MEMBER_INSTALLATIONS`). That renders the VMServiceScrape `storage-integrity-si-v2-members` (port `metrics` of the `si-member` Services, relabelled `network`, `si_component=member`, `release` and `member`) and the rule group `storage-integrity-si-v2.members`: `StorageIntegrityMemberUnscraped` (10m), `StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch` (critical, at once), `StorageIntegrityMemberForeignPart` (critical, at once), `StorageIntegrityMemberDiverged`, `StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind` (30m) and `StorageIntegrityMemberDiskHigh` (member disk above 50 %, 15m), each with its `runbook_url` into this file.

    echo "$s: $(si_vm_value "count(${s}{network=\"devnet2-si-v2\"})") series"
  done
  echo "DiskTotal_member: $(si_vm_value 'count(ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_DiskTotal_member{namespace="sentio-network-devnet2"})') series"
  si_vm_query 'ALERTS{alertstate="firing",alertname=~"StorageIntegrityMember.*"}' | jq -c '[.data.result[].metric]'
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/monitoring-members.txt"
grep -q '"group":"storage-integrity-si-v2.members"' "$si_backup/monitoring-members.txt" || { echo "vmalert has not loaded the members group: stop"; exit 1; }
tail -n 1 "$si_backup/monitoring-members.txt" | grep -qx '\[\]' || { echo "a member alert fires: read it (§14.1)"; exit 1; }
```

Expected: the group `storage-integrity-si-v2.members` with its six rules, each `"health":"ok"`; three members up (`member-a`, `member-b`, `member-c`); 6 series each of the shadow, foreign, diverged and copy-behind metrics (two peer owners per member); a `DiskTotal_member` series per pod of the three installations; and `[]`: no member alert fires.

## 9. Bootstrap

Each member starts with no copy and installs every Active table of both peer owners up to their latest published entry, every part checked by the install gate: the first part of each copy from the P1 backups by restore and every other part by owner pull. P1's backups are the bootstrap source (spec §8.6): while an owner has no journaled entry, the first fetch of each of its copies tries the restore before the owner pull, once per copy and member process (Plan S3-C2 contract §22.3, its bootstrap restore probe), so the restore count proves the member's restore key, `READ ON S3` and the bucket on devnet2 while the owner pull, the P2 order's first source, delivers the rest. Read-only, re-runnable; it waits up to six hours and records each member's state:

```bash
# block p2-9-1
{
  for n in $(seq 1 360); do
    if si_copies_check > "$si_backup/copies-bootstrap.jsonl" 2> /dev/null; then break; fi
    sleep 60
  done
  cat "$si_backup/copies-bootstrap.jsonl"
  for x in b c a; do
    echo "member-$x:"
    si_member_metrics "$x" 'sentio_node_si_member_(ready|copies|installs_total|install_outcomes_total|foreign_tables|diverged_partitions_total|diverged_tables|installs_paused|disk_used_bytes|disk_budget_bytes|audit_clean)'
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/bootstrap.txt"
tail -n 1 "$si_backup/copies-bootstrap.jsonl" | grep -qx 'copies equal: 6 of 6' || { echo "the copies did not reach the published entries within six hours: read bootstrap.txt (§14.1)"; exit 1; }
python3 -I - "$si_backup/bootstrap.txt" <<'EOF'
import re, sys
text = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
def total(pattern):
    return sum(float(v) for v in re.findall(pattern + r"(?:\{[^}]*\})? ([0-9.e+]+)$", text, re.M))
def each(name):
    return [float(v) for v in re.findall("^" + name + r"(?:\{[^}]*\})? ([0-9.e+]+)$", text, re.M)]
restore = total(r'^sentio_node_si_member_installs_total\{source="restore"\}')
pull = total(r'^sentio_node_si_member_installs_total\{source="owner_pull"\}')
problems = []
if restore <= 0:
    problems.append("no member installed from the P1 backups (installs_total{source=\"restore\"} is 0 on all three): the bootstrap restore probe of every copy missed or failed (§14.1)")
if pull <= 0:
    problems.append("no member installed by owner pull")
for name in ("sentio_node_si_member_foreign_tables", "sentio_node_si_member_diverged_partitions_total", "sentio_node_si_member_diverged_tables", "sentio_node_si_member_installs_paused"):
    if any(v != 0 for v in each(name)):
        problems.append(f"{name} is not 0 everywhere")
if each("sentio_node_si_member_ready") != [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] or each("sentio_node_si_member_audit_clean") != [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]:
    problems.append("a member is not ready with a clean audit")
for p in problems:
    print("FAIL:", p)
if problems:
    sys.exit(1)
print(f"bootstrap ok: installs from restore {restore:.0f}, by owner pull {pull:.0f}; no foreign or diverged copy; every member ready")
EOF
```

Expected: six JSON lines with `"equal": true` and `copies equal: 6 of 6`, then `bootstrap ok: installs from restore <n>, by owner pull <m>; no foreign or diverged copy; every member ready`, with `<n>` at most the number of copies (one probed part per copy) and `<m>` the rest. A Foreign or Diverged copy, paused installs or a missing restore: stop and follow §14.1.

## 10. Shadow soak

Spec §16 row P2 as amended (K38): on devnet2 every member shadow-verifies every block of its two peer owners sealed during a soak of at least 24 hours, with zero mismatches; the soak's writes spend at most half the promotion budget (§1.3); missed scans (a candidate part the owner cleaned before the member pulled it into `hg_rstage`) are counted apart and reported, and every owner has at least one block per write round that every member shadowed without a missed scan, so the byte scans ran; the copies stay at the latest published entry; the member disks stay below 50 %. The 500-blocks-per-owner volume and the Rejected-statement test are Plan S3-C2 Task 36's release-path full soak (`P2_INTEGRATION_SOAK`, §1.1 and §1.3), never re-run on devnet2: the consensus state grows about quadratically in promotions, so devnet2 cannot carry 500 blocks per owner.

The soak is: the start (read-only); round 1 at once, round 2 at least 12 hours and round 3 at least 24 hours after the start, each a read-only pre-round sample, one confirmed block of `k` writes per owner (owner 0 through indexer-a's sidecar, owners 1 and `INDEXER_C_ID` through the `devuser1` owner's agent in the user's own terminal, as in §1.3) and the read-only round check; sampling at any time; the end at least 24 hours after the start and after round 3's writes. Round `r` writes indexer-a's values `5202 + (r - 1)·k` to `5201 + r·k` and rows `2 + (r - 1)·k` to `1 + r·k` of both soak tables (`v` = `p2-10-<id>`); every owner's block appends to `soak-writes-<r>.txt` and leaves the marker `soak-writes-<r>-<owner>.done`, so a write never runs twice. Nothing else changes on devnet2-si-v2 during the soak: no sync, apply or pod deletion, no table-set transition (the shadow verifier skips those) and no other write drill (its promotions would count against this budget).

The start, read-only (it writes only local records; a second run prints the record and stops there). It computes `k` from `budget-start.txt` as §1.3 did, checks that the soak's `9k` writes still fit in half the budget after every promotion since §1.3, waits until every member's shadow verifier has passed the sealed tip, and records the start in `soak-start` and `soak-k`:

```bash
# block p2-10-1
if [ -s "$si_backup/soak-start" ]; then si_p2_member_identity_check && si_p2_vmalert_check || exit 1; echo "the soak started already:"; cat "$si_backup/soak-start"; exit 0; fi
grep -qx 'copies equal: 6 of 6' "$si_backup/copies-bootstrap.jsonl" || { echo "bootstrap has not finished (§9): stop"; exit 1; }
[ -s "$si_backup/p2-monitoring-commit" ] || { echo "the members are not monitored (§8.4): stop"; exit 1; }
line="$(tail -n 1 "$si_backup/budget-start.txt")"
B="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.*budget to L\/4 ([0-9]* bytes): \([0-9][0-9]*\) promotions;.*/\1/p')"
L0="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.*; live promotion \([0-9][0-9]*\);.*/\1/p')"
[ -n "$B" ] && [ -n "$L0" ] || { echo "budget-start.txt holds no estimator line (§1.3): stop"; exit 1; }
K=$(( (B / 2 - 3) / 9 ))
[ "$K" -le 3 ] || K=3
[ "$K" -ge 1 ] || { echo "a budget of $B promotions leaves no soak write (k=$K): stop (contract §27.7)"; exit 1; }
spent=$(( $(si_show | jq -r .promotion_seq) - L0 ))
[ $((spent + 9 * K)) -le $((B / 2)) ] || { echo "$spent promotions since §1.3 and $((9 * K)) soak writes exceed half the budget ($((B / 2))): stop (contract §27.7)"; exit 1; }
echo "budget room ok: spent $spent since the start, $((9 * K)) planned, half the budget $((B / 2))"
[ ! -e "$si_backup/soak-member-identities.jsonl" ] || { echo "partial soak identity evidence exists: stop and reconcile before a new start"; exit 1; }
si_p2_member_identities > "$si_backup/soak-member-identities.jsonl" || exit 1
si_p2_vmalert_pod_identity > "$si_backup/soak-vmalert-pod.json" || exit 1
si_p2_vmalert_identity > "$si_backup/soak-vmalert-identity.json" || exit 1
sealed="$(si_p2_sealed)"
for n in $(seq 1 90); do
  si_shadow_sample > "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv"
  awk -F'\t' -v l="$sealed" '$11 <= l {behind = 1} END {exit behind}' "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv" && break
  sleep 20
done
awk -F'\t' -v l="$sealed" '$11 <= l {behind = 1} END {exit behind}' "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv" || { echo "a member's shadow verifier is not past the sealed tip $sealed after 30 minutes: stop (§14.1)"; exit 1; }
[ "$(si_p2_sealed)" = "$sealed" ] || { echo "a block was sealed while the start was sampled: run this block again"; exit 1; }
awk -F'\t' '$5 != 0 {bad = 1} END {exit bad}' "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv" || { echo "a member counts shadow mismatches already: stop (§14.1)"; exit 1; }
version="$(si_status a devnet101 swap_new2 | jq -r .registry_version)"
[[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "no registry version from indexer-a: stop"; exit 1; }
cat "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv" >> "$si_backup/soak.tsv"
printf 'SOAK_START_UTC=%s\nSOAK_START_SEALED=%s\nSOAK_START_REGISTRY_VERSION=%s\nSOAK_K=%s\nSOAK_B=%s\nSOAK_L0=%s\n' "$(cut -f1 "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv" | head -n 1)" "$sealed" "$version" "$K" "$B" "$L0" > "$si_backup/soak-start"
printf '%s\n' "$K" > "$si_backup/soak-k"
cat "$si_backup/soak-start-sample.tsv" "$si_backup/soak-start"
```

Expected: `budget room ok: …`; six sample lines (`member-b` with owners 0 and `INDEXER_C_ID`, `member-c` with 0 and 1, `member-a` with 1 and `INDEXER_C_ID`), each with 0 mismatches, `behind_seconds` 0 and the shadow's next block above the sealed tip; and the six lines of `soak-start`.

Each round `r` (1, 2, 3) is five blocks; set `r` in each. First the pre-round checks and sample, read-only (a second run prints the sample taken):

```bash
# block p2-10-2
r=1
case "$r" in 1|2|3) ;; *) echo "r is 1, 2 or 3"; exit 1 ;; esac
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "$si_backup/soak-start"
si_p2_member_identity_check && si_p2_vmalert_check || exit 1
need=$(( (r - 1) * 43200 ))
elapsed=$(( $(date -u +%s) - $(si_epoch "$SOAK_START_UTC") ))
[ "$elapsed" -ge "$need" ] || { echo "round $r starts no earlier than $((need / 3600)) h after the soak start: $(( (need - elapsed) / 60 )) minutes to go"; exit 1; }
[ "$r" = 1 ] || grep -q '^round ok' "$si_backup/soak-round-$((r - 1)).txt" 2> /dev/null || { echo "round $((r - 1)) has not passed its check: stop"; exit 1; }
spent=$(( $(si_show | jq -r .promotion_seq) - SOAK_L0 ))
[ $((spent + 3 * SOAK_K * (4 - r))) -le $((SOAK_B / 2)) ] || { echo "$spent promotions since §1.3 and $((3 * SOAK_K * (4 - r))) writes still to come exceed half the budget ($((SOAK_B / 2))): stop"; exit 1; }
[ "$(si_status a devnet101 swap_new2 | jq -r .registry_version)" = "$SOAK_START_REGISTRY_VERSION" ] || { echo "the table registry moved since the soak start (a table-set transition inside the soak): stop and report"; exit 1; }
if [ -s "$si_backup/soak-round-$r-before.tsv" ]; then echo "round $r's pre-round sample was taken already:"; cat "$si_backup/soak-round-$r-before.tsv"; exit 0; fi
si_shadow_sample > "$si_backup/soak-round-$r-before.tsv"
cat "$si_backup/soak-round-$r-before.tsv" >> "$si_backup/soak.tsv"
cat "$si_backup/soak-round-$r-before.tsv"
echo "round $r ready: indexer-a values $((5202 + (r - 1) * SOAK_K)) to $((5201 + r * SOAK_K)), rows $((2 + (r - 1) * SOAK_K)) to $((1 + r * SOAK_K)) of both soak tables"
```

Owner 0's `k` writes through indexer-a's sidecar:

Confirm before running.

si_p2_member_identity_check && si_p2_vmalert_check || exit 1

si_p2_soak_budget "$SOAK_K" || exit 1

[ "$(grep -cE "^track $c published [0-9]+ -> [0-9]+\$" "$w")" = "$SOAK_K" ] && grep -qx "round $r owner c safe rows $lo to $hi: $SOAK_K" "$w" || { echo "owner $c's writes of round $r did not all reach safe: stop"; exit 1; }

A mismatch fires `StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch` as well: P2 stops; follow §14.1. ## 11. Measurements

Read-only. The soak's verdict (every sealed non-transition block of each peer owner shadowed by each member, every soak block evaluated with quorum, zero mismatches, the member disks below 50 %), the copies, the alert history and the members' cost to their hosts (spec §18: members compete with the SNode for CPU, memory and fetch threads):

```bash
# block p2-11-1
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "$si_backup/soak-start"
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "$si_backup/soak-end"
si_p2_member_identity_check || exit 1
start_epoch="$(si_epoch "$SOAK_START_UTC")"; end_epoch="$(si_epoch "$SOAK_END_UTC")"
seconds=$((end_epoch - start_epoch))
[ "$seconds" -ge 86400 ] || { echo "soak shorter than 24 hours: stop"; exit 1; }
hours=$(( ($(si_epoch "$SOAK_END_UTC") - $(si_epoch "$SOAK_START_UTC")) / 3600 + 1 ))
{
  si_blockowners "$((SOAK_START_SEALED + 1))" "$SOAK_END_SEALED" > "$si_backup/blocks-soak.jsonl"
  echo "blocks $((SOAK_START_SEALED + 1)) to $SOAK_END_SEALED: $(wc -l < "$si_backup/blocks-soak.jsonl" | tr -d ' ') sealed, per owner (non-transition): $(jq -s -c 'map(select(.transition | not)) | group_by(.owner) | map({owner: .[0].owner, blocks: length})' "$si_backup/blocks-soak.jsonl")"
  si_copies_check | tee "$si_backup/copies.jsonl"
  echo "StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind fired in the last 24 h: $(si_p2_vm_query_at 'count_over_time(ALERTS{network="devnet2-si-v2",alertname="StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind",alertstate="firing"}[24h])' "$end_epoch" | jq -c '[.data.result[].metric]')"
  echo "StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch fired in the soak: $(si_p2_vm_query_at "count_over_time(ALERTS{network=\"devnet2-si-v2\",alertname=\"StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch\",alertstate=\"firing\"}[${seconds}s])" "$end_epoch" | jq -c '[.data.result[].metric]')"
  si_p2_vm_range 'last_over_time(sentio_node_si_member_copy_behind_seconds{network="devnet2-si-v2",si_component="member"}[60s])' "$start_epoch" "$end_epoch" > "$si_backup/copy-lag-history.json"
  si_p2_vm_range 'timestamp(sentio_node_si_member_copy_behind_seconds{network="devnet2-si-v2",si_component="member"})' "$start_epoch" "$end_epoch" > "$si_backup/copy-lag-scrape-times.json"
  si_p2_py history "$si_backup/copy-lag-history.json" "$si_backup/copy-lag-scrape-times.json" "$start_epoch" "$end_epoch"
  si_p2_vmalert_history "$start_epoch" "$end_epoch"
  echo "copy lag series over the last 24 h: 6"
  for x in a b c; do
    if [ "$x" = c ]; then path=/var/lib/clickhouse-member; else path=/var/lib/clickhouse; fi
    df_line="$(si_kubectl exec "$(si_ch_pod "$x")" -c clickhouse -- df -B1 --output=size,avail "$path" | tail -n 1)"
    echo "member-$x disk: $path filesystem size, available: $df_line; used $(echo "$df_line" | awk '{printf "%.4f", ($1 - $2) / $1}')"
    echo "member-$x bytes on disk member: parts $(si_ch_admin "$x" "SELECT sum(bytes_on_disk) FROM system.parts WHERE disk_name = 'member'"), detached $(si_ch_admin "$x" "SELECT sum(bytes_on_disk) FROM system.detached_parts WHERE disk = 'member'")"
  done
  for x in a b c; do si_kubectl get pod "$(si_member_pod "$x")" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name} phase={.status.phase} restarts={.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="si-member")].restartCount}{"\n"}'; done
  si_vm_query "max by (pod) (max_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=\"sentio-network-devnet2\",container=~\"si-member|sentio-node\",pod=~\"sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-.*\"}[${hours}h]))" | jq -c '[.data.result[] | {pod: .metric.pod, max_working_set_bytes: .value[1]}]'
  si_vm_query "max by (pod) (max_over_time(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=\"sentio-network-devnet2\",container=~\"si-member|sentio-node\",pod=~\"sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-.*\"}[5m])[${hours}h:5m]))" | jq -c '[.data.result[] | {pod: .metric.pod, max_cores: .value[1]}]'
  si_vm_query "max by (pod) (max_over_time(ClickHouseMetrics_BackgroundFetchesPoolTask{namespace=\"sentio-network-devnet2\"}[${hours}h]))" | jq -c '[.data.result[] | {pod: .metric.pod, max_fetch_tasks: .value[1]}]'
  si_p2_py soak "$si_backup"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/measurements.txt"
! grep -q '^FAIL' "$si_backup/measurements.txt" || { echo "a soak criterion failed: stop (read measurements.txt)"; exit 1; }
grep -qx 'copies equal: 6 of 6' "$si_backup/copies.jsonl" || { echo "the copies are not at the latest published entries: stop"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind fired in the last 24 h: \[\]$' "$si_backup/measurements.txt" || { echo "StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind fired within the last 24 hours of the soak: stop"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch fired in the soak: \[\]$' "$si_backup/measurements.txt" || { echo "StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch fired: stop"; exit 1; }
grep -qx 'copy lag series over the last 24 h: 6' "$si_backup/measurements.txt" || { echo "the copy lag series do not cover the six member and owner pairs, so the alert could not have fired: stop"; exit 1; }
awk '/^member-. disk:/ {if ($NF + 0 >= 0.5) bad = 1} END {exit bad}' "$si_backup/measurements.txt" || { echo "a member disk's filesystem is 50 % used or more: stop"; exit 1; }
[ "$(grep -cE '^sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-[abc]-si-member-0 phase=Running restarts=0$' "$si_backup/measurements.txt")" = 3 ] || { echo "a member pod restarted during the soak (its counters were reset): stop and report"; exit 1; }
echo "measurements ok" | tee -a "$si_backup/measurements.txt"
```

Expected: the soak's blocks per owner; `copies equal: 6 of 6`; `[]` for both alert histories and `copy lag series over the last 24 h: 6` (the positive control, backed by copy-lag-history.json and its strict per-minute coverage verdict over the exact recorded soak window); each member disk's filesystem below `0.5000` used, with the member bytes; the three member pods Running without a restart; the members' and the hosts' peak memory, CPU and fetch tasks for the record; then the soak verdict's six lines `<member> owner <id>: shadowed +<n> of <m> sealed non-transition blocks, +0 mismatches, …`, its window line, `soak ok: …` and `measurements ok`. A block of a peer owner that a member did not shadow, a block without a verdict with quorum or a mismatch fails the verdict: stop and report.

## 12. End

The P2 exit (spec §16 row P2 as amended, K38) holds only if every criterion below holds, each from its own block; `p2-end.txt` records them, one line each from `(1)` to `(7)`, and its last line is `P2_END`, which this plan's live task records:

1. Plan S3-C2's integration soak: `P2_INTEGRATION_SOAK` is at least 500 and its Task 36 run record is the release-path full soak at `ARBITER_PIN_P2` with `TestPipeline_MemberShadowSoak` and the PASS line of `TestPipeline_MemberCopiesNeverHoldRowsOfARejectedStatement` (§1.1, §1.3; read again below).
2. Every member shadowed every sealed non-transition block of both peer owners in the soak, with zero mismatches, missed scans reported apart, and in every round at least one block per owner without a missed scan (§10, §11).
3. `StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind` never fired during the last 24 hours of the soak and the final `si_copies_check` printed `copies equal: 6 of 6` (§11).
4. Every member disk's filesystem is below 50 % used, with the member bytes recorded (§11).
5. As `si_member`, every row of the live probe is refused on all six SI ClickHouses, `CREATE TABLE … ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree` with 497 naming `TABLE ENGINE ON ReplicatedMergeTree` (the exit probe below).
6. The promotion budget read again at the end shows P2's promotions within half of `budget-start.txt`'s budget (below).
7. The soak tables are dropped and every member dropped its copies of them (Retiring on; below).

## 13. Rollback

P2 changes no consensus state, so every step can be undone; the order is the reverse of what ran, and a step that has not run has no commit file and is skipped. Every revert is one confirmed block: `si_p2_revert` reverts that commit on a freshly fetched `origin/main` (refusing a conflict with a later commit, which means a later step must be reverted first), runs the render tests, pushes, then applies the CHI manifest (`kubectl apply`, server dry run first) or syncs the one release; after a pushed revert it only applies again. Three things stay: the member ids (allocated for good), `unsafe_inc` (never removed, K42) and `table_engines_require_grant` once a restart carried it, unless the user decides to pay another restart.

A member (any order among the three; the host is untouched, and its StatefulSet, ConfigMap and Service go):

Confirm before running.

```bash

x=b
case "$x" in a|b|c) ;; *) echo "x is a, b or c"; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ -f "$si_backup/p2-monitoring-commit" ] && [ ! -f "$si_backup/p2-monitoring-commit.reverted" ]; then echo "revert member monitoring first using its block below: stop"; exit 1; fi
si_p2_revert "p2-member-member-$x-commit" "release:sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x"
for n in $(seq 1 30); do si_p2_assert_absent pod "$(si_member_pod "$x")" && break; sleep 10; done
si_kubectl get pod "$(si_member_pod "$x")" --ignore-not-found
si_p2_host_state "$x"

Irreversible: deleting the member state PVC and its databases loses the saved journal and copies. Stop unless the user explicitly confirms that loss after the member pod is proved absent. si_kubectl delete pvc "si-member-state-sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-si-member-0" --wait=true
si_ch_admin "$x" "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS hg_replica SYNC"
si_ch_admin "$x" "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS hg_rstage SYNC"
```

  mv "$si_backup/restart-watch-$chi.txt" "$saved"
fi
si_p2_revert "p2-restart-$inst-commit" "$target"
si_restart_watch "$chi" "$si_backup/chi-$inst-revert-before.txt" | tee "$si_backup/restart-rollback-$inst.txt"
awk -v want="$(grep -c '^pod ' "$si_backup/chi-$inst-revert-before.txt")" 'NF != 4 || $2 != "restarts" || $3 != "seen:" || $4 != 1 {bad=1} END {exit bad || NR!=want || want==0}' "$si_backup/restart-rollback-$inst.txt" || { echo "rollback restarted a pod other than exactly once: stop"; exit 1; }
for h in $hosts; do si_p2_stage_check "$h" engines; done
```

## 14. Operating rules

### 14.1 Members

- A member is off consensus in P2: a member that is down, stuck or removed affects no track, no verdict and no promotion. Restarting a member pod is safe at any time; it audits its copies at startup (spec §8.7), and again whenever its ClickHouse's uptime regresses, and resumes from its install journal.
- `StorageIntegrityMemberForeignPart` (critical): a fetched part matched no needed row hash and is no split, rename race or doubled retry. The member keeps the scratch table in `hg_rstage` for forensics and quarantines that copy locally; page, investigate the transport (which owner or peer served the part, from the member's log), never delete the scratch before the investigation ends, and clear the quarantine only then with `sentio-node si-member clear-foreign --table <database>.<table>` inside the member's container while the member is stopped (Plan S3-C2 K36); the copy is rebuilt at the next start.
- No install from restore at bootstrap (§9): every copy's bootstrap restore probe (Plan S3-C2 contract §22.3) missed, was refused or found the store unreachable, and the owner pull filled the copies instead. Read `sentio_node_si_member_install_outcomes_total` and the member's log (`install: no source delivered a part; deferred` names each source's outcome only when the owner pull failed too): `missed` means no backup index of the owner lists the copies' first parts (a table created after the newest backup of `owner-<id>/`, or parts the owner rebuilt since); `refused` or `unreachable` points at the member's restore Secret, `READ ON S3`, the bucket or the endpoint. The probe runs once per copy and process, so after the cause is fixed only a member that bootstraps again (a new state directory) probes again; record the finding and ask the user before going on.
- `StorageIntegrityMemberDiverged` (warning): a copy holds a part the manifest does not list; the member rebuilds that partition by itself (a fresh scratch, `DROP PARTITION`, `ATTACH PARTITION FROM`; never `REPLACE PARTITION`). Page if it repeats for the same table.
- `StorageIntegrityMemberShadowMismatch` (critical): the member's own replay or byte scan disagrees with the recorded evidence of a block. P2 stops: no further write round runs; keep the member running, record the block (`si_blockowners <seq> <seq>`) and the member's log, and escalate. A shadow mismatch changes no verdict, because the member submits nothing.
- `StorageIntegrityMemberCopyBehind` (warning, 30 minutes): the copy has stayed behind the latest published entry; read the member's `installs_paused`, its install outcomes and the owner's reachability. Installs pause by design when the member's bytes cross `stop_installs_ratio` × `disk_budget_bytes` (half the member disk); `StorageIntegrityMemberDiskHigh` fires when the member disk's filesystem crosses 50 %. Free space on the node SSD or end P2; never raise the ratio.
- `StorageIntegrityMemberUnscraped`: the member's metrics are not scraped; read its pod and Service.
- Residuals accepted in P2 (K43, contract §25.9): on the network installation `si_member`, its collection grants, the collections, the reader environment, the `member` disk and the bundle files also exist on the three verifier ClickHouses, which no si-member uses; the network installation's `si_member` password lives only in `member-a`'s Secret; the reader passwords in the ClickHouse containers' environment, and in each ClickHouse's preprocessed `config.xml`, are readable by anyone who can `kubectl exec` into those pods, the same exposure as the admin Secrets; `default`, an admin on loopback, can read the collections. Interserver credentials, NetworkPolicies, the Keeper allowlist and node pins are stage 3 P4's.

### 14.2 Engine grants after the restart

From an installation's restart on, a `CREATE` whose engine its user does not hold is refused with 497 (`TABLE ENGINE ON <engine>`). The answer is always to grant that engine by name, a users reload, never to turn `table_engines_require_grant` off (that costs every installation another restart) and never `ON *`. A `Replicated*` engine is never granted to `si_gateway`, and `si_snode` and `si_verifier` keep exactly `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`; a 497 of a protocol user means its code path changed and stops everything until the plan is amended. A tenant engine is granted before its first use where possible. For a tenant engine the 497 names, set `engine` and run, one installation per window, the engines-style commit for each installation in turn (indexer-b, indexer-c, network), each with its own confirmed push and apply and the read-only grants check of §4:

```bash
# block p2-14-2-1
engine=SummingMergeTree
inst=indexer-b
case "$inst" in network) chi=storage-integrity-si-v2 ;; indexer-b|indexer-c) chi="storage-integrity-si-v2-$inst" ;; *) echo "inst is network, indexer-b or indexer-c"; exit 1 ;; esac
[[ "$engine" =~ ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ ]] && [[ "$engine" != Replicated* ]] || { echo "$engine is no tenant engine name"; exit 1; }
si_p2_fresh
engines="$(python3 -I -B -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "charts/storage-integrity/tests"); import test_render as t; print(",".join(t.DEVNET2_GATEWAY_ENGINES))')"
case ",$engines," in
  *",$engine,"*) echo "DEVNET2_GATEWAY_ENGINES holds $engine already: only $inst's file changes" ;;
  *) si_p2_py constant DEVNET2_GATEWAY_ENGINES - "$(printf '%s,%s' "$engines" "$engine" | tr ',' '\n' | sort -u | jq -R -s -c 'split("\n") | map(select(. != ""))')" ;;
esac
stage="$(python3 -I -B -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "charts/storage-integrity/tests"); import test_render as t; print(t.DEVNET2_P2_STAGE[sys.argv[1]])' "$chi")"
si_p2_yaml "$inst" "$stage"
git diff --stat | cat
python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py 2>&1 | tail -3
```

Then commit it with `si_p2_commit "chore(devnet2): grant TABLE ENGINE ON $engine to si_gateway on $inst (users reload)" "<why: the 497 that named it>" <the changed files>`, and push and apply it in a confirmed block as §4 does.

### 14.3 ClickHouse restarts

- From P2 on, every planned restart of an SI ClickHouse (a CHI change that restarts pods, a node drain, a pod deletion) is a window of §5's shape: the quiet point first (`si_quiet_point`, which includes Plan S3-B runbook §13.3's check for inactive `hg_safe` parts), one installation at a time, never combined with another change, then the owner audit's clean `clickhouse_restart` run, and for the network installation every block of the window evaluated with quorum.
- A restart carries the bundle again from the CHI; nothing in it has to be re-applied. The members re-audit their copies when their ClickHouse's uptime regresses; their installs resume afterwards.
- An unplanned restart: read `sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_clickhouse_restarts_total` and `runs_total{trigger="clickhouse_restart"}` (one more each) and `unclean_tables` on the owner, the members' `audit_runs_total{trigger="clickhouse_restart"}`, and `si_p2_stage_check` on that host; a finding is handled as the stage-3 P0 runbook's §13.3 says.
- A pod that restarted more than once in a window, or a window whose watch timed out, stops P2 and requires the user to review before another window. Read `$si_backup/restart-watch-<CHI>.txt` and the operator's log, wait for the CHI to settle, then run the window's read-only checks; never start the next window before they pass.

### 14.4 Promotion budget

Every drill that writes on devnet2 from now on computes its budget first with `si_budget_capture` and `si_budget` (Plan S3-B runbook §13.4 as merged in housegate#237) and spends at most half of it; churn drills run in the integration environment or on a partitioned throwaway table. Read the budget again after the drill (`budget-end.txt` here): the state the drill left is what the next drill starts from, and the voters' 2Gi memory and volume do not grow by themselves (spec §13.1).
````

```bash
# The session helpers as the P2 runbook's §0 says to define them: depth first along the runbooks its §0 links, each
# runbook's first bash block of §0, found by its fences line by line (decision D24).
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

FENCE = re.compile(r"(`{3,})([^`\s]*)\s*$")


def section_zero(path):
    lines = path.read_text().split("\n")
    intro, block, fence = [], None, None
    for line in lines[lines.index("## 0. Session helpers") + 1:]:
        if fence is None:
            opening = FENCE.match(line)
            if opening:
                fence = opening.group(1)
                if opening.group(2) == "bash":
                    block = []
            elif line.startswith("## "):
                break
            else:
                intro.append(line)
        elif re.fullmatch(re.escape(fence) + r"`*\s*", line):
            if block is not None:
                return re.findall(r"\]\((storage-integrity-devnet2-[a-z0-9-]+\.md)\)", "\n".join(intro)), "\n".join(block) + "\n"
            fence = None
        elif block is not None:
            block.append(line)
    sys.exit(f"{path}: no bash block in section 0")


def collect(docs, name, seen, out):
    if name in seen:
        return
    seen.add(name)
    earlier, block = section_zero(docs / name)
    for other in earlier:
        collect(docs, other, seen, out)
    out.append((name, block))


out = []
collect(Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], set(), out)
for name, block in out:
    print(f"# --- §0 of docs/{name}")
    print(block, end="")
print("chain: " + " ".join(name for name, _ in out), file=sys.stderr)
PYEOF
bash -n "$selftest_root/chain.sh"
export HOME="$selftest_root/home"
mkdir -p "$HOME"
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source "$selftest_root/chain.sh"

  declare -F "$f" > /dev/null || { echo "missing helper $f"; exit 1; }
done
[ "$si_backup" = "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p2" ] && [ "$si_p2_logins_dir" = "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p2-logins" ] || { echo "si_backup or si_p2_logins_dir is not the runbook's"; exit 1; }
echo "the §0 chain sources; every helper of contract §27.2 is defined"

import sys

heading, want = sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
current, fence, body, found = None, None, None, []
for line in lines:
    if fence is None:
        m = re.match(r"(`{3,})([^`\s]*)\s*$", line)
        if m:
            fence, body = m.group(1), ([] if m.group(2) == "bash" and current == heading else None)
        elif re.match(r"#{2,3} ", line):
            current = line
    elif re.fullmatch(re.escape(fence) + r"`*\s*", line):
        if body is not None:
            found.append("\n".join(body) + "\n")
        fence, body = None, None
    elif body is not None:
        body.append(line)
if len(found) < want:
    sys.exit(f"{heading} has {len(found)} bash blocks, not {want}")
print(found[want - 1], end="")

}
```

**Conventions for this task.**
- **Session, frozen source and block files (contract §28.3, D24).** Task40 creates `$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p2-session` (mode700); Task41 reuses it. Step2 runs `prepare.py init` once after the actual public ledger inputs were read: it freezes Task39's actual declared P2 ancestor chain, the complete P2 runbook, the two probe corpora and the exact helper/P/ledger suffix. The chain is derived from §0's declared links and first Bash block, not a forecast count; future P3/P4/P5/P6 books are refused. The ten existing ancestor helper overrides are explicit; any extra helper collision fails. A source/helper/ledger/corpus change stops before the next block, never silently refreshes the snapshot.
- **Runbook blocks are prepared, never copied by heuristic.** The unique first line `# block p2-<section>-<ordinal>` is the block's identity; subsection/ordinal references below are an audit aid and must match the frozen marker map. Use `$S/task40/prepare.py block "$S" <marker> 40-<nn>-<what>` to emit an exclusive `blocks/40-<nn>-<what>.sh` plus `.json` source/rendered-hash metadata. It does not execute. Every prepared file reconstructs its full bytes from the frozen source plus only declared pins/round/key-path substitutions, checks the exact marker/body metadata before sourcing any helper or body, and claims execution atomically. A metadata-only round change or body+hash co-edit cannot change the execution identity. A confirmed mutating marker can be attempted once across labels; a round block's identity is marker+round, so each of rounds1/2/3 may run once. A read-only block can run again only from a new label. A `.started` without a successful actual exit receipt is an unknown outcome: stop and investigate, never automatically rerun or generate a new mutating label.
- **Execution and receipts.** After any required actual chat confirmation, run the prepared file with `bash -eo pipefail "$block" < /dev/null`, preserving combined stdout/stderr in `$block.out` and the actual status in `$block.exit`. The wrapper must refuse preexisting output/status files; use `rc=0; bash -eo pipefail "$block" < /dev/null > "$block.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$rc" > "$block.exit"; cat "$block.out"; test "$rc" = 0` in its fresh Bash call. Do not call `claim` externally: the generated file self-claims immediately before helpers/body. `check-block` is read-only and may be used before asking for confirmation. No heredoc wraps a runbook block. Long windows/polls run in the background and their actual result is read before proceeding. Owner blocks run only through the user's wrapper, which uses the same frozen producer and captures its own exit/transcript; the agent never executes them.
- **This task's supplemental blocks.** Steps1/2 bootstrap their own fresh files as specified. Later supplemental blocks of this task are written once to new `blocks/40-<nn>-<what>.sh` files: select Python3+PyYAML, run `prepare.py check "$S"` first, source `helpers.sh` then `task40/task40.sh`, and `cd "$P" || exit1` before the quoted body. Preserve their actual output/status as above. Never edit or reuse a file after execution. Tasks41's labels start41, avoiding collision.
- **The runbook decides, this task acts.** "Run runbook §X's block k" means: prepare the unique matching marker from the frozen subsection/ordinal map, preserving its complete body verbatim; the only declared substitutions are §1.1's three pin/path lines from the actual ledger and, in user mode only, the single key_file path line (and an explicitly declared round line in Task41). Each runbook block's checks, stops and Expected text are the runbook's (D19); where this task adds a read-only check it says so and gives its output. If the runbook and this task disagree on what is changed (a file, a value, an installation, an order), stop and report before running either.
- **Explicit user confirmation.** Every remote or live mutation waits for an explicit yes in chat, given for that block only, and each step says so: the copy of the tools into the voters' containers, every staging block that applies, writes Keeper, runs a refused statement or deletes, each push to production `main` with its `kubectl apply` or `helmfile sync`, each restart window, each 497 probe, each acceptance write (indexer-a's by the agent, the `devuser1` owner's by the user), the Keeper write of `UNSAFE_INC_ROOT`, the member probe, any revert, and the housegate push, PR and merge. Before asking, the agent states that block's Gate sentence, saying exactly what will change; for a push it also shows `git -C "$P" show --stat --oneline HEAD` and the `t40_change` output. Read-only blocks (`kubectl get`, `describe` and `logs`, an `exec` that only reads, the `si_*` read helpers, `git fetch`, `gh pr view`, local files) need none.
- **The user's terminal.** The user makes every password, token and Secret with `make-p2-logins.sh` (Step 4) and runs the `devuser1` owner's four blocks (Steps 5, 11, 12) with `t40-user-block.sh`, both in their own fish terminal; the agent never runs either and never sees a key (the key file's path is not the key). Passwords and tokens never appear in chat, on argv or in a log: the runbook's `si_ch_admin`, `si_ch_exec`, `si_member_ch` and `si_p2s_ch` pipe them from their Secrets into `kubectl exec -i` stdin, and Secrets are read only as key names and sizes (`kubectl describe`). Commands handed to the user are fish.
- **One window per step.** Steps 8–17 are one window each: one installation per window, and a restart (Steps 11–13) never rides with any other change (K39). After each window's closing check, report the window and end the turn; the next window starts only when the user asks for it in a later turn (contract §27.5: never two windows in one session). Between Step 3 and Step 19 run no other sync, apply or pod deletion against devnet2-si-v2's installations, hosts, verifiers or voters, no consensus update, no Plan S3-D interserver or node-pin change, no other write drill (its promotions would count against the budget) and no helmfile against `k8s-sea/clickhouse` (K22).

The runbook's local block of each stage (§4, §5, §7) makes the commit on the live checkout's detached HEAD (`si_p2_fresh`, `si_p2_yaml`, the render tests, `si_p2_commit`); `t40_change` checks it; the runbook's confirmed block pushes it as `HEAD:main` after `si_head_is` and applies or syncs. A local block or a `t40_change` that stops leaves an unpushed commit or edits: drop them with a block of `git reset -q --hard origin/main` (local only; it was never pushed) and report. A confirmed block whose `si_head_is` stops (`main` moved) has pushed nothing: drop the local commit the same way, run the local block and `t40_change` again from new files, and ask again. A push rejected by GitHub is never forced.
- **Stop rules.** Stop on any unexpected output and report it; never improvise a fix on the cluster, never edit a test, a template or a manifest by hand. Above all: a census `FAIL:` line (K41; a protocol user's finding means its code path changed and the plan is amended; a tenant replicated table without pinned merges is the user's decision, K39); a staging outcome other than runbook §3's (a restart at an engines or member stage, an override answered other than 36 `Override not allowed for '<key>'`, a znode left by a refused replicated `CREATE`, a grant-probe row other than its `expect`); a quiet point that does not come (§14.3); a pod that restarts at an engines or member stage, or not exactly once at its restarted stage; an owner audit `clickhouse_restart` run that is not one clean run; any 497 for a protocol statement after a restart; a tenant 497 (P2 stops; on the user's decision runbook §14.2 grants that engine by name in reviewed engines-style commits, which `t40_change` does not cover, so the user reviews each `git show` before its push); a block sealed in the network window without a verdict with quorum, or a quarantined track; an epoch other than `ENROLMENT_EPOCH`; a member-probe row that is not refused; any `t40_change` refusal. A window that fails after its apply: report at once and ask for runbook §13 (each revert is its own confirmed block; a restarted stage's revert is another restart, only on the user's decision, at a quiet point). A watch that times out is not a failure in itself (runbook §14.3): read `$si_backup/restart-watch-<CHI>.txt`, wait for the CHI to settle, then run the window's read-only checks; never the next window before they pass.

```python
prepare.py user SESSION MARKER LABEL KEY_PATH [ROUND]
```
